name: i-have-adhd
description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
one_liner: A set of rules you add to your AI coding assistant so it gives short, numbered, action-first answers instead of long rambling explanations.
buyer: Nobody pays cash for this directly today — it's a free tweak for developers' own AI tools, not a product with a paying customer.
business_use_cases: A solo developer installs it to cut the time they spend scrolling past preamble in AI chat responses — a personal productivity tweak, not a sale.
A coding-assistant vendor borrows the same prompt-style rules as a built-in 'concise mode' feature to differentiate their product.
An accessibility consultant cites it as a reference implementation when advising companies on ADHD/neurodivergent-friendly software design.

money_ideas.idea: There isn't a real monetizable business here as a standalone product; the closest option is folding the concept into a paid 'accessible AI tooling' consulting practice.

steal_this: Fork it, tune the rules to your own taste, and share the result on your dev blog to build an audience — not a business, but a nice credibility piece.
